text:
Connor McDavid has 58 points in 26 games, and 45 of them are assists. He plays 23.7 minutes a night, has 27 power-play points, and with him on the ice at 5v5 Edmonton takes 59.8% of the shot attempts.

Some of it is running hot. He has 13 goals on 9.8 expected (expected goals measure the quality of his chances), shooting 19% against 16% last season, and the Oilers have scored 25 more goals than expected with him out there. Our talent range puts his true scoring rate near 4.46 points per 60, below the 5.65 he is posting.

His point streak ended Nov. 19 in Tampa, and Edmonton followed with a 7-4 loss in Carolina, where he had no shots, and an overtime loss in St. Louis. Over ten games he has 18 points against 19.7 expected: a normal stretch by his standard.

The engine hasn't changed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 68% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him first among 401 forwards at 4.4 wins above replacement, the year he won his sixth Art Ross.
